title: Geniocracy as the canon's proposed government
statement: The canon proposes geniocracy — a selective democracy weighting political participation by measured intelligence, reserving candidacy and franchise to those above stated thresholds — delivered as the first of the New Commandments in the 1973 contact; this record carries the proposal as the canon's explicit normative content, together with the standing objections to it, without the corpus endorsing or operationalizing it.

includes: The proposal as the canon states it: the selective-democracy structure, its intelligence thresholds, and its placement as the first New Commandment
Its provenance and rank within the canon's normative program (delivered in the 1973 contact recorded by woh-claim-0020)
The reception layer: the measurement, rights, and historical-abuse objections to intelligence-gated franchise, carried at full strength as the mainstream position
excludes: Endorsement; the corpus records the canon's proposal and does not advocate it
Operationalization: no measurement instrument, threshold procedure, or implementation path is specified or defended
Any claim that intelligence measurement is settled science; the psychometric dispute is part of the reception layer
The movement's political activity around the proposal, which is organizational history

source_references.locator: The New Commandments: the geniocracy commandment and its thresholds as stated
The academic treatment of the geniocracy doctrine and its reception

alternatives.statement: Intelligence-gated franchise violates political equality, the core commitment of democratic theory; the proposal is anti-democratic in the term's ordinary sense despite its self-description.
No instrument measures the political-relevance intelligence the proposal requires; psychometrics cannot carry the gate.
Capacity-gated franchise has a documented abuse history; the proposal's safeguards are unspecified.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0020 is revised in a way that affects the provenance.
The canon's fuller context changes the proposal's content or rank.
Public prose begins endorsing, operationalizing, or soft-pedaling the objections, all of which this record excludes.
